_comment: HAND-AUTHORED SPECIFICATION FIXTURE — MODULES.json M1, DESIGN.md §8, risk R7.
Three FrameState values, authored by hand against fixtures/plan.reference.json. This
is what lets M4 be built and visually tuned BEFORE M2 computes a single step: the
renderer needs a frame to paint, not a planner, and FrameState is owned by M1 so M2 and
M4 never negotiate a type. That is R7 closed — the base design named FrameState 'the
seam that makes the two biggest modules parallelizable' and then never typed it.
The three samples are chosen to be the three visually distinct regimes, not three
arbitrary clock readings:
mid-head   2070ms   step 0, halfway through a 4140ms dwell. ONE lane. The sides have
not faded in yet: opening on three lanes is overwhelming, so the
sides arrive at the head->middle transition and the center is the
thread held the whole way (§5.3). The threshold's master fade is
still climbing, so masterAlpha is 0.72 rather than 1.
mid-peak   38688ms  step 10, halfway through a 2988ms dwell — the deepest content
at the curve peak and the tightest pacing, with both sides in
`named`. THREE lanes, and this is the frame that has to prove the
center is unambiguously dominant (C1): center scale 1.0 alpha
1.0, sides scale 0.55 alpha 0.30. A renderer that gets this frame
right gets the whole session right.
mid-tail   67500ms  step 19, halfway through a 3791ms dwell. ONE lane again. The
sides faded out at the middle->tail transition — closing on three
lanes is jarring. Both would be in `first` if they were showing
at all: the person axis has been handed back before the visual
one closes.
Per-lane facts and where they come from:
alpha        composited: the envelope's value multiplied by the lane's stratification
(§5.2). Center 1.0, sides 0.30 — three full-alpha layers just show
whichever drew last, and it is the stratification that makes the stack
legible. All three samples are taken mid-dwell, at the envelope's hold,
so the values here are the plateau rather than a ramp.
active       the `.active` gate (§5.2). Every draw is AND-ed with it. An INACTIVE
lane paints nothing at all — it is not kept around at zero opacity
waiting to flash. That is why the head and tail frames carry `active:
false` sides with empty text rather than omitting the channels: the
shape of FrameState is constant, and the gate is what varies.
scale/blur   §5.3. Center 1.0/0, sides 0.55/slight.
split        center LINE, sides WORD (§5.2). The center is read whole; the sides
seep one token at a time.
text         ALREADY SUBSTITUTED — this is what gets painted, so {subject} has become
Alex and {controller} Morgan, per config.reference.json. `template` keeps
the raw form beside it so a renderer can re-substitute without reaching
back into the plan. In the mid-peak frame the sides are mid-drain and so
show a single WORD token while the center shows its whole LINE — the
anchor/periphery distinction has a temporal dimension on top of alpha,
scale and blur.
holdMs       an inline [500]/[1.5s] pause marker's hold. Zero throughout: the mini
corpus authors none, and a nonzero value here would be inventing corpus
content inside a renderer fixture.
progress     elapsedMs / contentMs (69396), clamped. Drives the backdrop uniforms.
bed          §1.4. pulseHz stays well under the ~3Hz ceiling (§5.6) and is shared
with the backdrop so visuals and entrainment run off one clock.
The bed is quieter and slower at the bookends than at the peak.
ended        true only once the last token has drained AND the tail has run out.
False in all three samples, including mid-tail: at 67500ms there are
1896ms of content plus 2500ms of quiet plus a 1500ms fade still to go.
